intended_object: The irreducible character χ^μ of the symmetric group S_n attached to a partition μ of n, i.e. the character of the Specht module S^μ, viewed as an integer-valued function on S_n. This comes from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The definition returns `FDRep.intCharacter (spechtModule μ)`. `FDRep.intCharacter V g` is defined as `(V.character g).num`, the numerator of the rational character value. The lemma `intCharacter_cast` proves that this numerator, cast back to ℚ, equals the character, so the character is integer-valued and taking the numerator loses nothing.

`spechtModule μ` is the rational Specht module: the span of the polytabloids of μ-tableaux inside the permutation module M^μ. It is moved from permutations of the diagram's cells to `Fin n` along the size equality `card_ofPartition`. This is the standard construction, as in James and in Sagan.

So for every σ, `spechtChar μ σ` equals χ^μ(σ) = tr(σ | S^μ), as an integer. This is a specific object (the character of the Specht module of a partition of n), so it is not too narrow. Working over ℚ is enough, since S^μ is defined over ℚ, and S_n characters are rational, in fact integral.

Mathlib has no Specht modules and no symmetric-group character, so there is no Mathlib counterpart.
